rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: a candidate move is a move worth calculating. In positions with an exposed king or a loose piece, start the list with checks, captures and threats to a piece.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.e2: Game Binoop1111 vs aragors, Lichess. Black is a piece up, and the knight on c4 is attacked by your pawn on b3.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.e3: Forcing moves come first: the knight checks on f6 and e7, the queen captures on g7 and d6, the rook capture on f7 and the pawn capture on c4. Threats, such as attacking the queen on h5, come after.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.p: Calculate Black's reply to each candidate and play the one that wins.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes: the knight gives check on f6 and attacks the queen on h5. The pawn on g7 cannot take it, because it is pinned by your queen on g3.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.revela: The winning move is the knight check on f6: it attacks the king and the queen on h5, and the pawn on g7 is pinned by your queen on g3.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.b3c4.1: The pawn captures the knight on c4 and wins the piece back.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.b3c4.2: The black queen goes to e5 and offers a queen trade. The game is level, and another candidate wins more.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.volta: Back to the position: calculate the other candidates on the list.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.d5e7.1: The knight gives check on e7, but from there it attacks no other piece.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.d5e7.2: The king goes to h7, and the check won nothing.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.g3g7.1: The queen captures the pawn on g7 with check.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.g3g7.2: The king captures the queen: the check gives up the queen for a pawn.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.f1f7.1: The rook captures the pawn on f7 and attacks the rook on f8.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.f1f7.2: The queen on h5 recaptures on f7: the capture gives up the rook for a pawn.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.g3d6.1: The queen captures the pawn on d6.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.err.g3d6.2: The knight on c4 recaptures: the capture gives up the queen for a pawn.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.fora: That move is not on the list of checks, captures and threats. Calculate the candidates.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.l.1: The knight gives check on f6 and attacks the queen on h5 at the same time: it is a fork. The pawn on g7 is pinned by the queen on g3.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.l.2: The king only has h8: the knight on f6 also attacks h7.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.l.3: The knight captures the queen. Black was a piece up, and now White is ahead in material.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.l.4: The other candidates did not work: taking on c4 only wins the piece back, the check on e7 wins nothing, and the captures on g7, d6 and f7 give up material with no forcing blow after.
rot.candidateMoves.ideia.ex1.l.5: In positions like this, with the king and queen exposed, the list had six candidates, and only calculating each one showed the fork.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.descoberta.1: Attack: still White, now making the list together. Game Hussaini786 vs RayL, Lichess, from a Caro-Kann. The black queen on d4 has no defender, and your bishop on d3 stands between it and your queen.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.descoberta.l.1: The checks and captures are three: the bishop takes on h7 with check, the bishop takes the knight on f6, and the knight takes the pawn on d5.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.descoberta.l.2: Calculate the first: the bishop captures the pawn on h7 with check and leaves the d-file. Now your queen attacks the black queen.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.descoberta.l.3: The knight captures the bishop to get the king out of check. If the king captured or went to h8, the queen on d4 would fall all the same.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.descoberta.l.4: Your queen captures the queen on d4.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.descoberta.l.5: The other candidates did not work: with the knight off c3, the bishop on b4 captures your queen, and taking on f6 wins nothing.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side. Game realPioneer vs skyfaller1, Lichess 2021. Your queen on g3 is close to the white king.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.l.1: Start with the queen checks. On h2, on f2 and capturing on g2, it would be captured with no forcing blow after. The check on e1 is different: no white piece attacks that square.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.l.2: The queen goes to e1 with check, and the king only has h2.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.l.3: The king goes to h2, its only square.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.l.4: Make the list again: the bishop captures the pawn on e5 with check. In positions like this, one forcing candidate opens the way for the next.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.l.5: The pawn goes to g3 and blocks the check, because the king has no free square.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.l.6: The queen captures the pawn on g3 with check, defended by the bishop on e5.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.l.7: The king goes to h1, its only square.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.xeques.l.8: The queen captures the bishop on f3 with check. Black has won a bishop and two pawns, and the attack goes on.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.1: Attack: back to White. Game zazaiaganashvili2011 vs adidas17, Lichess. Black is a pawn up, and your queen on h6 is close to the black king.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.l.1: The list has seven candidates: five queen checks, the knight capture on a4 and the rook capture on d5.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.l.2: The most natural check: the queen captures the pawn on g6.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.l.3: The black queen on d6 recaptures: the check gives up the queen for a pawn, and no forcing blow follows.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.volta: Back to the position: the other checks also give up the queen with no forcing blow after, and the two captures win nothing. No candidate on the list works.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.c.1: In positions like this, look for the quiet move too: the rook goes to h3, with no check and no capture, and threatens mate with the queen on h8 and the rook on h7.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.c.2: The king runs to f7 to escape the mate.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.c.3: The queen gives check on h7, protected by the rook on h3.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.c.4: The king goes to f6. On f8, the queen and the rook would give mate; on e8, the mate would come with the knight's help.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.c.5: The rook goes to h6 and attacks the pawn on g6, which shields the king. To escape mate, Black will have to give up material.
rot.candidateMoves.demos.excecao.c.6: Here no check or capture worked, and the right move was quiet. The short list is the start of calculation, not the end.
The knight uncovers the check, but it does not attack the queen on g3. The king steps out of check, and White stays ahead in material. Look for the check that also attacks the queen.
You win the bishop back, but the chance is gone. There is a knight check that wins the queen.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.valeAqui.enun: Now let us think from Black's side. Does it work here? Make the list of checks and captures, calculate each one and play the one that wins.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.valeAqui.fim: The knight gave a double check on e2 and attacked the queen on g3. After the king stepped out of check, the knight captured the queen.
The knight uncovers the check and attacks the queen on g3, but the queen goes to f2, blocks the check and offers a trade.
The knight captures the pawn on f3 with a discovered check, but the queen on g3 stays free. There is a check that also attacks the queen.
After this move, the queen on g3 captures the pawn on c7 with check, and White stays ahead in material. There is a knight check that wins the queen.
The rook captures the pawn on h3, but the queen on g3 recaptures with check.
The queen on g3 is still attacked by your knight: capture it.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.xequeDama.enu: Back to White. Black is a piece up, and the black king on g8 has few defenders. Make the list of checks and play the one that wins.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.xequeDama.fim: The queen gave check on e8 and then on g6. Next, the rook goes to f7 and threatens mate, and Black gives up the queen to defend.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.xequeDama.err: The queen gives check on f7, but the queen on d5 captures it.
The queen gives check on e6, but the queen on d5 captures it.
The queen captures the pawn on g7 with check, but the king captures it.
The rook gives check on f8, but the knight on d7 captures it.
The queen gives check on f8, but the knight on d7 captures it.
The queen captures the knight on d7, but the bishop on c8 recaptures.
The knight leaves e5, and the rook on e3 captures your queen.
The knight captures the pawn on c6, but Black stays a piece up.
The rook goes to f7 without giving check. Black answers with the rook to g3 and threatens mate with the queen on g2.
The queen gives check on d8, but the king goes to h7, and the check leads nowhere.
That gives the black king time. The queen has another check that keeps the attack going.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.desvio.err.to: After this move, the rook on e1 captures your rook on e8 with check. Start with the captures with check.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.desvio.err.da: The queen gives check, but it gets captured. Look for another candidate.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.desvio.enunci: Still Black. Make the list of checks and captures and play the best move.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.desvio.fim: The rook captured the rook on e1 with check, and the queen on d1 recaptured and stopped defending f3. This is deflection: after it, your queen captured the bishop.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.desvio.err.h3: The queen on d1 recaptures on f3. Remove that defender first.
rot.candidateMoves.pratica.desvio.err.po: That wins little. After the recapture, the bishop on f3 was left undefended.
